question: A project shared across a department has no named owner. Several people hold edit access and each has added documents over the past year. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Edit access is revoked automatically after a long period of inactivity, so the project becomes read-only.
B) Shared projects reset their instructions whenever a second person saves a change to the knowledge.
C) Each new document replaces the previous one, so the project only ever holds the most recent upload.
D) Nobody is accountable for removing outdated material, so contradictory documents accumulate unchecked.
correct_answers: D) Nobody is accountable for removing outdated material, so contradictory documents accumulate unchecked.
explanations: Access is not withdrawn on its own because a project has been quiet.
Editing knowledge does not clear the project's instructions.
Uploads accumulate; they do not overwrite one another.
Correct. Shared editing without ownership is precisely how a knowledge base fills with conflicting versions.
